The Book of Common Prayer (1559) retained sixteen-member electronic witness3907571f9368082a0f45e2aba8d4c36d0503a7931631d690ee5dc700d336591eOne existing complete16-member retained electronic expression, not a pure or fully collated1559 print edition. Preserve all declared member text/tables/inline source context and their internal order in one TEI; source table of contents and its links retained independently from inventory ordering. Keep1561/1604 and later State Prayer variants explicit. Godly Prayers is explicitly never officially part of BCP but often bound with it, from1567/1599/1634 sources; preserve it as a declared contextual appendix, not silently drop or create newworkIDs. James I proclamation is expressly later1604 context (own imprintAnno1603); Commination standalone overlapping Churching member retained separately as declared witness context. Undeclared PDFs/HTML/assets are outside immutable primary16 selection.Fifteen retained HTML footers explicitly credit Charles Wohlers as Web author; the standalone Commination member does not carry that footer. The inherited Richard J. Mammana transcription claim remains unconfirmed and is not asserted as current attribution. The provider Notes on the Text state that these HTML pages were transcribed from The Prayer Book of Queen Elizabeth 1559, published in 1890 by Griffith Farran Okeden and Welsh (Griffiths 1890/7), which in turn appears to use Richard Grafton's London 1559 book. The provider identifies an original 1634 edition for the 1604 changes and consulted John Booty (1976), William Keeling (1851), and Frank Streatfeild (1950) for specified contexts. These are retained provider statements, not independent print collation.All 16 declared member bodies retain their exact decoded text/tails, ordered hierarchy, and original HTML attributes in reversible source annotations. All 128 HTML tables (391 rows and 998 cells) are represented, including web-navigation, title-banner, layout, and content relationships; this does not classify every HTML table as a liturgical data table. The calendar alone contains 35 tables. Five source blocks under inline font/b wrappers use closed inline carriers without flattening or changing their source hierarchy. Source font/class/color/size/align attributes remain explicit annotations, not inferred speaker identities, rubric classifications, or response links. The HTML numeric-reference decoding rule renders 90 literal • references as bullets and two † references as daggers; their original byte locations and lexemes remain accounted. The two dagger occurrences form the Confirmation prayer/footnote marker pair. Source head/prolog/comment material and exact outside-html whitespace are accounted separately. HTML recovery assumptions are disclosed; no browser or print collation is claimed.All 53 literal image occurrences, alt attributes, and original link targets remain represented as source-context references. The retained _index.html and PDF1623.htm files are outside that selection and remain supplementary evidence, not added primary members.
